Person/target binding and investigation traces are not such technical validation operations or AI package metadata.

review.reason_for_change: Unauthorised package publication is reported, but no content manifest, SPDX AI metadata or CycloneDX model-card reference governed by this requirement is identified.

review.requirement_proposition: Preserve decisions, assumptions, data choices, evaluation results and mitigation rationales relevant to bias.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: 3.4.1 concerns bias-related data/decisions/evaluation records, not target-collision or credential/release compromise traces.

review.reason_for_change: The intrusion does not identify a bias-governance process or bias-evaluation record.

conclusion_change.previous: Untrusted issue content crossed into a tool-enabled workflow and then propagated through shared infrastructure into release authority. The model interaction was one necessary link; cache design, token scope and release configuration were independently necessary. Prompt authority, control-plane propagation and captured reconstruction retain their roles. The recovery decision is also assessed as target-binding failure because the wrong token was deleted while the exposed token remained usable. Later correct revocation does not erase that interval; OpenClaw is not recast as malicious.
conclusion_change.new: The documented chain crossed from untrusted issue text through AI tool execution and shared infrastructure into release authority. Security failed. Bounded traceability, incident documentation and later repair are supported. The wrong-token revocation interval remains distinct, and full audit and monitoring arrangements remain unresolved.
